headlines.title_en: Trump's posts cost $100K/month for early access, frequently naming listed companies
headlines.summary_en: According to the Associated Press, Truth Social, owned by U.S. President Trump, launched a high-speed information service called 'Truth API' on August 1 local time, charging Wall Street trading institutions for rapid access to Trump's social media posts, raising questions about insider trading, conflicts of interest, and using public office for private gain. Reports say the Truth API costs up to $100,000 per month, targeting mainly high-frequency trading firms. Since Trump often uses Truth Social to announce tariffs, wars, central bank leadership changes, and other major policy news, these posts frequently trigger rapid fluctuations in stocks, bonds, exchange rates, and commodity prices. Critics argue that even if posts are theoretically released to the public simultaneously, paying clients could exploit faster data interfaces and automated trading systems.

headlines.title_en: Power outages in multiple Cuban provinces
headlines.summary_en: Cuba's Electric Union reported on August 1 that at 18:07 local time, a power outage occurred across the system from Matanzas Province to Pinar del Río Province. The Union stated on social media that the outage was caused by a line trip. Due to U.S. sanctions, Cuba has long struggled to import fuel and power plant equipment, with aging facilities difficult to upgrade, straining the national power supply. Since October 2024, Cuba has experienced multiple nationwide blackouts due to equipment failures, hurricanes, and other causes. (CCTV News)

headlines.title_en: US government advises American citizens in Middle East to prepare for evacuation
headlines.summary_en: According to CCTV, on August 1 local time, the U.S. State Department issued a broad security warning to American citizens in the Middle East, advising them to 'consider leaving the area, or be prepared for rapid evacuation if tensions escalate.' Per earlier reports, U.S. officials revealed that Washington is considering launching a new round of military strikes on Iran as early as this weekend. Meanwhile, Iran has also stated it will further strike countries that allow U.S. troops to be stationed at military bases. The State Department again reminded people in the Middle East to remain cautious and vigilant, while being prepared for flight cancellations, temporary airspace closures, and other travel disruptions. The advisory also emphasized that American citizens planning to travel to the Middle East should seriously reconsider their plans.

headlines.summary: 当地时间7月31日，美国财政部长贝森特在参加马里兰州戴维营举行的内阁会议期间表示，按照特朗普总统的指示，财政部持续对伊朗展开经济攻势，并且正在全球范围内追查伊朗资产。他还特意在特朗普面前罗列对伊朗的所谓“经济战果”：2025年3月推进相关行动后，当年年底伊朗最大民营银行宣告破产，伊朗央行被迫大量印钞，不断推高通胀，贝森特声称，如今伊朗甚至无力支付军饷。这番言论立刻引来网友质疑和吐槽。（央视）

headlines.title_en: US Treasury Secretary says pursuing Iranian assets globally
headlines.summary_en: On July 31 local time, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent said during a Cabinet meeting at Camp David in Maryland that, following President Trump's instructions, the Treasury continues its economic offensive against Iran and is tracking down Iranian assets worldwide. He even listed so-called "economic achievements" against Iran before Trump: after advancing related actions in March 2025, Iran's largest private bank went bankrupt by the end of that year, forcing the central bank to print money heavily and pushing inflation higher. Bessent claimed Iran is now unable to even pay military salaries. The remarks immediately drew skepticism and mockery from netizens. (CCTV)
